An update on building games with Claude Code:

Last week some of you ran into Claude Code pushing back on game projects it should have just built. We'd added a short rule to the Opus 5.5 prompt to steer Claude away from recreating specific existing games, but it was also kicking in when you referenced one just to describe the mechanics you wanted.
 
We've updated that rule in 2.1.317. You can name a game to describe what you want and Claude should now build an original game in that genre. If you ask for a copy of the original, it'll offer to build something similar instead.
 
We want Claude to be as helpful as possible when you're building something original, but also to protect your work if someone else tries to copy it. We'll keep improving this, so let us know if Claude turns down work that's yours. Thanks to everyone who shared feedback!

#ClaudeCode #Codex #AIエージェント #セキュリティ

AIエージェントが書いたコードのうち、機能と安全性を両立できていたのは、最大でも4分の1程度だったことが報告されました。

Alibaba Groupなどの研究チームによる報告です。

バイブコーディングでは、入力値のチェックや権限管理といったセキュリティ上の判断を、AIが利用者に伝えないまま決めています。利用者は動作確認で済ませがちなので、脆弱性は見逃されやすくなります。

しかも、コードの安全性を測る既存のベンチマークは、対象が関数単位だけ、特定の言語だけ、特定の種類の脆弱性だけといったものが中心でした。

研究チームは、実在する150件の脆弱性をもとに、7言語・24種類の脆弱性タイプを含む450タスクのベンチマークを提案しました。

具体的な仕組みは以下の通りです。

・3段階の出題範囲：1件の脆弱性から、関数の穴埋め、ファイル単位、ゼロからの構築の3つのタスクを作成

・安全性に触れない仕様：仕様書にセキュリティの指示は書かず、AIが自分で気づいて対処できるかを確認

・AIに見せないテスト：機能テストと、攻撃を再現するセキュリティテストの両方で採点

主要な6つのモデルに450タスクのコードを書かせて採点したところ、仕様どおりに動くかを見る機能テストの合格率は73.6〜91.3%でしたが、機能と安全性を両立できたタスクは16.4〜25.1%にとどまりました。

たとえば、アーカイブの取り込み機能は、通常のファイルでは正しく動いても、細工したファイルで展開先の外に書き込めてしまうことがあります。機能テストだけでは、こうした脆弱性は見つかりません。

ただし、この結果は仕様にセキュリティの指示を含めない条件のものです。
また、同じ脆弱性をもとにした3つのタスクのうち、1つで防げても他では防げないことが多く、入力のターン数を増やしても安全性は上がりませんでした。

動作確認が通るだけで済ませず、攻撃を再現するセキュリティテストも別に用意することが有効かもしれません。

Zero Wireは、Cloudflare Radarに加わった重大な脆弱性を調べるための公開の情報フィードで、米国時間11/3に発表された。
Radarのセキュリティ欄にあり、1件ごとのブリーフィングに、平易な説明、調べるべき人、推奨される対応、証拠とベンダー情報へのリンクがまとまる。
対象は、Webアプリやそのランタイム、ライブラリなど、インターネットに公開されたソフトウェアの重大なCVEである。
すべてのCVEを並べるのではなく、ベンダーのアドバイザリや脆弱性データベースを補う位置づけである。
トップページは、積極的な評価や対応が必要な「Needs attention」と、情報が落ち着いた「Reference」に分かれる。
Cloudflareの顧客でなくても使える情報だと説明されている。
自分のエージェントに渡して影響範囲を評価させる、プロンプトも用意されている。
このプロンプトは読み取り専用の評価を求めるもので、コピーしただけではシステムのスキャンも変更も行われない。
WAFルールで緩和できる場合はその提供状況も示されるが、WAFは補完的な対策であり、ソフトウェアの修正の代わりにはならない。
脆弱性の公開直後に、情報収集の入口を1か所にできる点は、セキュリティ担当の負担を下げると思う。

#Cloudflare #CloudflareRadar #脆弱性

Max, Homebrew is the best argument against this post.

Last year I wrote a paper scoring 100 install methods. On macOS:

Homebrew Core: 89/100
Homebrew Cask: 84/100
A developer's own curl | sh: 43/100
A third-party curl | sh: 18/100

That's a 46 to 71 point gap on the same Mac. People who flinch at curl one-liners are reacting to that gap, even if they can't explain it.

You're right that it comes down to trust, and you're right that a proper package manager is what you want. Afaik, where we differ is that I don't think trust is a yes/no question about the vendor. When you run curl | sh, you trust the vendor, their domain, their DNS, their CDN, and whoever holds their GitHub token on the day you install. You can't verify what you got, you can't tell if everyone else got the same file, nobody can revoke it, and nothing records what ran.

The paper I wrote scores six things. Integrity and review/CI are worth 25 points each, provenance and least privilege 15 each, update hygiene and distribution hygiene 10 each. curl | sh gets 0 out of 25 on review and between 1 and 8 out of 25 on integrity.

You said you can at least inspect the script before running it.

The file your browser shows you and the file curl downloads can be different. The server sees the User-Agent and sends whichever it wants.

With | sh the server can do more. The shell runs the script while it's still downloading, so the server can tell from the timing that the output is going into a shell and send a different payload. http://idontplaydarts.com published a working demo of this 10 years ago. It even beats the careful version where you curl the script to your terminal first, read it, and then pipe it into sh, because the server can tell those two requests apart.

If the connection drops halfway, sh runs the half it received.

To run the exact script you read, you have to save it to a file, read the file, and run that file. That isn't a one-liner anymore, and once you add a hash check you've built a package. Most people never read the script anyway, since skipping that step is the reason one-liners exist.

You said a .pkg can also run arbitrary scripts.

Of course it can. The difference is that a pkg is a fixed file. The developer signs it with a Developer ID, Apple notarizes it, and Gatekeeper checks both before it runs. Suspicious Package shows you the same bytes the installer will run, and Apple can revoke the signature if the pkg turns out to be malware.

curl | sh runs whatever the server sends at the moment you press enter. HTTPS tells you that you reached the right domain. It tells you nothing about whether someone broke into that domain. Many of these scripts also call sudo partway through, so a script nobody read gets root.

You said MitM is a risk with any download.

A signature check fails if anyone changes the file in transit or on a mirror. That is the reason signing exists.

You said that once anything is installed it can run arbitrary code anyway.

After install, yes. But the install step decides whether you got the same file as everyone else, and whether anyone would find out if you didn't.

A curl | sh server can send malware to one company's IP range on one night and the clean script to everyone else, including any researcher who checks. A notarized pkg is one build with a hash Apple has on file. Releases signed through a transparency log like Sigstore leave a public record of every version, so a one-off malicious build would show up there. Most of supply chain security is about whether someone can send you different code without anyone noticing.

The inspect argument also assumes a person reads the script. In 2026 a lot of install commands get run by coding agents that copied them from a README, and the person's only check is approving a prompt. Nobody reads the script in that setup, so the install method has to be safe on its own.

Homebrew also ships a signed, notarized Homebrew.pkg on its GitHub releases. The current maintainers already built what the people complaining about curl asked for.

If you ship a CLI and want a better score:

- Put it in a package manager like a Homebrew tap, apt, winget, or nix. You get checksums and pinned versions with no extra work.
- Sign your releases. On macOS that means Developer ID plus notarization, and on other platforms cosign or minisign.
- If you still offer a curl command, pin the version, check a hash or signature inside the script, wrap the script in a main() function so a cut-off download runs nothing, install into the user's home directory, and ask before using sudo.
- Document how to verify the download. Most users will skip it, but anyone auditing your tool will use it.

You don't need to apologize for the one-liner. It got a lot of people to open a terminal for the first time, and in 2009 Gatekeeper, notarization and Sigstore didn't exist yet. Now they do, and the default install command should use them.

The paper is in the reply. I'd like to hear what you think.

There is a false equivalence being made between open source software and AI benchmarks.  

The argument is that  we shouldn't expend effort criticizing benchmarks, and should instead improve them. 

Unlike OSS software, benchmark results are consumed for decision making at face value.  They are currently used like Yelp or a credit score, and less like a informative dataset you can analyze

Benchmarks don't come with disclaimers, and people don't realize how brittle they can be.  Consumers don't have the data skills to analyze the traces and see the limitations of benchmarks.  Hell people who have the skills don't question it either, and are SHOCKED when they see the traces. 

So yeah, I think more people should have healthy skepticism.  Right now, most people don't realize what they are looking at.  The biggest problem is the large dissonance between the marketing of benchmarks and what they really measure.  

Instead of deflecting the criticisms of benchmarks, I think the communications need to be fixed around them.
